headline: Every major sits below its 200-day line, and fear is the honest emotion for it
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it settles most arguments before they start. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, and ADA are all below their 200-day averages, none has a golden cross, and BTC itself is 49% off its 12-month high of $124,773.51. When seven-for-seven agree on trend, that's not noise, that's the market's actual posture. ETH is the one asset showing any separation from the pack: RSI at 56.3, up 1.81% on the week and 6.36% on the month, even while still under its long-term average. That's a coin recovering inside a downtrend, not a coin in an uptrend. Worth naming, not worth overstating.

Momentum against trend is where the story gets interesting. BTC's RSI at 47.4 with MACD below signal is a market resting, not accelerating, in either direction. DOGE and BNB show MACD above signal despite sitting below their 200-day lines, a short-term pop inside a longer downtrend. That's a divergence: momentum flickering green while the trend underneath stays red. SOL's RSI at 42.7 alongside a 4.01% weekly loss says the selling has been orderly, not panicked, since RSI hasn't collapsed toward oversold territory. Nothing here screams capitulation. It looks more like drift.

Positioning tells a cleaner story. BTC funding on OKX sits at 0.0051% per 8 hours, annualized to 5.6%, a mild cost for holding long exposure, paired with a long/short ratio of 2.2. That's a crowd leaning long but not paying much for the privilege: not expensive, not crowded to the point of fragility. SOL and XRP funding have actually flipped negative (-3.6% and -0.3% annualized), meaning shorts are paying longs there, an unusual tell in a market where price is still soft. DOGE stands out at 5.49 long/short ratio and 7.0% annualized funding, the most crowded and priced long of the group, with liquidation flow already showing shorts taking more damage (33,389 vs 14,764 in longs) over the past 22 hours. Crowded and expensive is fragile; DOGE fits that description better than anything else on the board.

Flows are where sentiment and money start to disagree. BTC spot ETFs printed -$56.2m on 14 Aug, extending to -$385.2m over the last five sessions with three straight days in the same direction, a real outflow, not a blip. ETH ETFs went the other way: +$5.9m on 13 Aug, +$46.6m over five sessions, though same_direction_days of 2 means that trend is younger and shouldn't be leaned on too hard. Whale activity over the last 48 hours shows $62.6m in BTC net moving onto exchanges (specifically to Coinbase), plus $149.8m in USDT parked at Bitfinex, commonly read as dry powder rather than a sell signal. But the weekly whale-flow series tells the fuller story: three positive weeks (+$445.9m, +$1,075.3m, +$67.2m net off exchanges) followed by the most recent week at -$507.9m, a reversal into onto-exchange flow. Stablecoin float is essentially flat, down 0.4% over 30 days to $306.5b, so the sidelines aren't growing or shrinking meaningfully.

Sentiment reads Fear at 34, sitting at the top of its own 30-day range of 25 to 34. So the crowd has been fearful for a month and is, if anything, marginally less fearful today than at points in that window. That's roughly in line with the tape: BTC outflows from ETFs, whale coins moving onto exchanges this week, funding modest rather than manic. No real gap between what the crowd feels and what the money is doing today, which is itself worth noting given how often those two disagree.

What to watch: whether BTC ETF flows turn positive and break the three-day outflow streak, whether the weekly whale flow reading flips back to net outflow from exchanges after this week's -$507.9m print, and whether DOGE's stretched long/short ratio (5.49) and rich funding (7.0% annualized) resolve through a funding reset or a liquidation cluster on the long side. Any of those would mark a change from today's picture of a market resting below trend, mildly long, and quietly fearful.
